title: A dominant morphism of integral curves with finite generic extension is quasi-finite
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. Let $C$ and $E$ be integral [def-pc-integral-scheme] separated schemes of finite type over $k$, each of dimension $1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $p:E\to C$ be a dominant $k$-morphism that is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and induces a finite extension $k(C)\subseteq k(E)$ of function fields [def-sc-function-field]. Then $p$ is quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite] at every point of $E$.

source.place: Tag 0AB6 (lemma-quasi-finite-in-codim-1), condition (1) and proof: a locally finite-type morphism over a one-dimensional Noetherian target with finite generic residue-field extensions is quasi-finite over every target point.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-scheme-sober] to each of the irreducible schemes $E$ and $C$ (integrality gives irreducibility by [def-pc-integral-scheme]), obtaining unique generic points $\eta_E$ and $\eta_C$. For either scheme $X$, every point $x\ne\eta_X$ is closed: otherwise choose $z\in\overline{\{x\}}\setminus\{x\}$. Closures of singletons are irreducible. The uniqueness clause of sobriety makes $\overline{\{z\}}\subsetneq\overline{\{x\}}$, since equality would make $z$ and $x$ generic points of the same irreducible closed subset. Also $\overline{\{x\}}\subsetneq X$, since equality would make $x=\eta_X$. These two strict inclusions form a chain of length $2$, contradicting $\dim X=1$ by [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Finally $\eta_X$ is not closed: otherwise $X=\overline{\{\eta_X\}}=\{\eta_X\}$ would have dimension $0$. Thus the points of each curve are its generic point and its closed points.

source.place: Tag 01IS (lemma-scheme-sober), combined with Topology Tag 0055 (definition-Krull); the displayed length-two contradiction is the elementary dimension-one specialization argument.

proof.text: The morphism $p$ sends $\eta_E$ to $\eta_C$. Indeed, continuity gives $p(E)=p(\overline{\{\eta_E\}})\subseteq\overline{\{p(\eta_E)\}}$. Dominance says that $p(E)$ is dense in $C$, so $\overline{\{p(\eta_E)\}}=C$. The uniqueness of $\eta_C$ from Step 1 gives the assertion.

source.place: Tag 0AB6 (lemma-quasi-finite-in-codim-1), condition (1), specialized to a dominant map of integral curves; generic-point identification by continuity and density.

proof.text: If $x$ is closed in $E$, then $p(x)$ is closed in $C$. Put $y=p(x)$. By part (a) of [lem-kun-closed-point-field], $\kappa(x)$ is finite over $k$, since $E$ is of finite type over $k$. By [def-weil-residue-field], $p$ induces an injective field homomorphism $\kappa(y)\to\kappa(x)$; it is a $k$-homomorphism because $p$ is a $k$-morphism. Hence $\kappa(y)$ is a $k$-vector subspace of the finite-dimensional space $\kappa(x)$ and is itself finite-dimensional over $k$. Apply the converse in part (a) of [lem-kun-closed-point-field] to the finite-type $k$-scheme $C$: $y$ is closed.

source.place: Tag 0478 (lemma-locally-finite-type-Jacobson), part (1), and Morphisms Tags 01TE (lemma-algebraic-residue-field-extension-closed-point-fibre) and 01TF (lemma-closed-point-fibre-locally-finite-type), applied to the structure morphisms; elementary subfield argument.

proof.text: Fix $y\in C$. If $y=\eta_C$, Step 2 puts $\eta_E$ in $p^{-1}(\{y\})$. No other point lies there: by Step 1 any other point is closed in $E$, hence has closed image by Step 3, whereas $\eta_C$ is not closed. Thus this fibre set is the singleton $\{\eta_E\}$. If $y\ne\eta_C$, then $y$ is closed by Step 1, so continuity makes $F=p^{-1}(\{y\})$ a closed subset of $E$. Step 2 excludes $\eta_E$ from $F$; Step 1 therefore makes every point of $F$ closed in $E$. Apply [lem-kun-finite-closed-subscheme] with $X=E$ and this closed subset $F$: $E$ is of finite type over $k$, and all points of $F$ are closed, so $F$ is finite. This includes an empty fibre. Every fibre set of $p$ is consequently finite.

source.place: Tag 0BA8 (lemma-Noetherian-irreducible-components), the finite-components input to lem-kun-finite-closed-subscheme; finite type over a field is Noetherian by Morphisms Tag 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian).

proof.text: For every $y\in C$, apply [pqf-lem-locqf-fibre-discrete] to $p$ and $y$. Its hypotheses are exactly the assumed local finite type of $p$ and the finiteness of $p^{-1}(\{y\})$ proved in Step 4. It concludes that $p$ is quasi-finite at each point over $y$. Taking $y=p(x)$ for each $x\in E$ proves that $p$ is quasi-finite at every point of $E$, as required.

source.place: Tag 01TH (lemma-quasi-finite-at-point-characterize), the finite-fibre specialization recorded by pqf-lem-locqf-fibre-discrete.

lean.note: The finite function-field extension is RingHom.Finite for the canonical stalkMap at genericPoint E; dominance identifies p(genericPoint E) with genericPoint C, and the generic stalks are the recorded integral-scheme function fields. The conclusion uses the recorded Stacks IsQuasiFiniteAtPoint predicate, not Mathlib QuasiFiniteAt alone.
